claim: Wikipedia's WikiProject AI Cleanup guide treats a post-2022 edit that contains many 'AI vocabulary' words, repeatedly, as one of the strongest tells for AI use; one or two of them may be coincidental.
quote: lots of them, lots of times, is one of the strongest tells for AI use. The words that LLMs overuse have changed over time.
title: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing

claim: The Wikipedia guide reports that the word 'delve' was overused by ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024 and then dropped off sharply in 2025, so a word list ages as models change.
quote: early 2024, but became less frequent later in 2024, then dropped off sharply in 2025.
title: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing

claim: The Wikipedia guide's list of words typical of the newest model era (labelled 'Mid-2026 and on (GPT-6)') includes 'leverage', 'foster', 'dependable' and 'multifaceted'.
quote: Mid-2026 and on (GPT-6): challenge , clearer , dependable , echoed , foster , leverage ,
title: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing

claim: The Wikipedia guide gives 'seamlessly' within a sample of AI-generated promotional text, among a promotional-language word list that includes 'boasts', 'vibrant', 'rich' and 'enhancing'.
quote: seamlessly connecting the beginning and end of every traveller's journey
title: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing

claim: The Wikipedia guide says LLMs overuse the rule of three, in forms from 'adjective, adjective, adjective' to 'short phrase, short phrase, and short phrase'.
quote: overuse the rule of three . This can take different forms, from " adjective , adjective , adjective " to " short phrase , short phrase , and short phrase ".
title: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing

claim: The Wikipedia guide says AI em dashes often mimic punched-up sales-like writing, and that the sign is most useful in combination with other indicators.
quote: LLMs especially tend to use em dashes in a formulaic, pat way, often mimicking "punched up" sales-like writing by over-emphasizing clauses or parallelisms.
title: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing

claim: The Wikipedia guide says some AI companies have tried to suppress em dashes in newer chatbots, most notably OpenAI's GPT-5.1, which weakens em-dash counting as a detector for recent models.
quote: companies have attempted to make their newer chatbots suppress their use, most notably OpenAI's GPT-5.1 .
title: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing

claim: The Wikipedia guide lists section-closing summary phrases ('In summary', 'In conclusion', 'Overall') as words to watch.
quote: Words to watch: In summary , In conclusion , Overall ...
title: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing

claim: A summary of the Wikipedia guide (FlowingData, 2025-10-20) quotes its caveat that the list is not a ban on words or punctuation and that not all text with the indicators is AI-generated.
quote: This list is not a ban on certain words, phrases, or punctuation.
title: Signs of AI writing on Wikipedia

claim: tropes.fyi, a single-author catalog of AI writing tropes, calls the 'It's not X -- it's Y' pattern the most commonly identified AI writing tell (author's assertion; no measurement given).
quote: The single most commonly identified AI writing tell.
title: Negative parallelism - Tropes

claim: tropes.fyi gives a rule of thumb that a human writer might use 2-3 em dashes per piece while AI uses many more (author's assertion; no measurement given).
quote: A human writer might use 2-3 per piece (and naturally); AI will use a lot more.
title: tropes.md - Tropes

claim: Barron's, as reported by Fortune (2026-04-24), counted the 'it's not X, it's Y' construction in 208 documents from large US companies in 2025, against 100 in 2024 and 49 in 2023.
quote: Barron’s spotted this phrasing in 208 documents last year, up from 100 in 2024 and 49 in 2023.
title: AI in corporate communications: The "it's not X, it's Y" phrase giving CEOs away

claim: Fortune reports an AI detection company calling the 'it's not X, it's Y' phrase 'no smoking gun for AI use', and Schwab said its flagged quote was 100% human-generated (a false-positive case for this pattern).
quote: Schwab told Barron’s that the quote it identified was “100% human-generated.”
title: AI in corporate communications: The "it's not X, it's Y" phrase giving CEOs away

claim: Landing Doctor, a landing-page audit vendor, lists seamless, powerful, robust, intuitive, end-to-end and AI-driven as the abstract vocabulary of an 'AI-slop value prop' (vendor view, undated).
quote: feature soup built from abstract nouns and adjectives — powerful, seamless, AI-driven, end-to-end, robust, intuitive — with no concrete before/after.
title: Why AI-Generated Landing Pages Convert Worse (and the 6 Fixes That Move the Needle)

claim: Landing Doctor names invented testimonials, placeholder logos in the logo bar and unsourced precise statistics (such as 'trusted by 10,000 teams') as the tell of 'hallucinated or borrowed proof' on AI-built landing pages (vendor view, undated).
quote: invented testimonials, placeholder logos still sitting in the bar, or a precise stat with no source
title: Why AI-Generated Landing Pages Convert Worse (and the 6 Fixes That Move the Needle)

claim: Landing Doctor names generic headlines such as 'Streamline your workflow' and 'The modern platform for teams' as a tell, defined as a headline that could belong to any company in the category (vendor view, undated).
quote: the headline could belong to any company in the category — "The modern platform for teams," "Streamline your workflow," "Built for the way you work."
title: Why AI-Generated Landing Pages Convert Worse (and the 6 Fixes That Move the Needle)

claim: Superdesign (2026-07-13), a design-tool vendor, lists the 'mad-lib headline' of the form 'The AI-powered [X] for modern [Y]' as the first of six generic tells of AI landing pages.
quote: The mad-lib headline. "The AI-powered [X] for modern [Y]." It describes a category, not a promise.
title: Fix a Generic AI Landing Page: 6 Tells and the Prompts That Kill Them

claim: Superdesign names three-clause benefit copy such as 'Save time. Work smarter. Scale faster.' as a tell of AI landing pages, and a fixed section order of hero, logos, three features, testimonial, pricing, CTA.
quote: Benefit copy that could belong to anyone. "Save time. Work smarter. Scale faster." True of every product, specific to none.
title: Fix a Generic AI Landing Page: 6 Tells and the Prompts That Kill Them

claim: A peer-reviewed study (Liang et al., 2023) found that GPT detectors consistently misclassify non-native English writing as AI-generated, a false-positive risk for any stylistic detector of AI text.
quote: Our findings reveal that these detectors consistently misclassify non-native English writing samples as AI-generated, whereas native writing samples are accurately identified.
title: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers
